A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the CDM is a powerful model for describing choice behavior in concurrent chains with variable schedules, and that the value-added model is a good model for fixed schedules, but not as good as the CDM.
the CDM, when appropriately specified, can account for the effects of terminal-link schedules on choice in concurrent-chains schedules.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the CDM provides the most parsimonious account of choice in concurrent chains with heterogeneous schedules, and the most accurate predictions of choice in concurrent chain procedures with homogeneous schedules.
the CDM is an excellent model for concurrent chains, and it can be modified in a straightforward way to accommodate systematic deviations in data.
the CDM is an important step forward in the development of a comprehensive model of concurrent chains.
